name: AI Deep Dive — RKLB — 2026-05-31
rationale: Rocket Lab (RKLB) is a pure-play small-satellite launch and space systems company growing revenue at +63.5% YoY (TTM $601.8M). Analyst consensus projects ~51% growth in 2026 and ~41% in 2027. However, the stock trades at 138x revenue and $143.48/share — already 38% above the analyst mean price target of $103.91 — while remaining deeply unprofitable (TTM net margin -32.9%). The Neutron medium-lift rocket remains unproven and pre-revenue, representing a massive binary catalyst that either validates the bull thesis or destroys the growth narrative. Our fundamental DCF (10% discount rate, 5-year horizon) yields a weighted fair value of $10.46 — implying the current price embeds 13+ years of hypergrowth priced in simultaneously, with zero margin of safety for execution risk.

bear.rationale: Bear case: Electron launch cadence grows modestly (+18% CAGR) but Space Systems margins stall amid component cost pressures and Neutron capex burn. Company reaches breakeven (0% net margin) only by Year 5 — no PE-based exit value can be computed at zero earnings. The $0 present value in this scenario reflects that a zero-margin business at 35x PE generates no EPS to multiply. Historical trough: RKLB operated at -74.6% net margin in 2022 — the risk of re-widening losses from Neutron cost overruns is real. Sharecount dilution of +3.5%/yr assumes continued equity raises at current pace.
risks: Neutron development delay extends beyond 2028, competing directly with SpaceX Falcon 9 pricing power
Continued share dilution at pace exceeding revenue growth destroys per-share value
Macro risk-off rotation abandons high-multiple pre-profitability growth names; 138x P/S mean-reverts aggressively

base.rationale: Base case: 5-year CAGR of 28% derived from analyst consensus trajectory (Y1=+51.4%, Y2=+40.8%, Y3~+28%, Y4~+20%, Y5~+15%) — the hypergrowth exception applies per skill rules. Analyst consensus Y1=$910.8M, Y2=$1,282M. By Year 5 revenue reaches ~$2.1B. Gross margin expansion trend (9%→21%→26.6%→34.4%) extrapolates toward 40%+ gross margins enabling 7% net margin by Year 5 — consistent with early-phase Industrials/Aerospace best-in-class (Benchmark: 2-12% typical, 15% best-in-class). Exit P/E of 60x reflects a space-tech premium, anchored below SpaceX private comps but above sector median (18x) for a hypergrowth transitional company. Quality multiplier 1.0 — one moat source (Electron/photon platform + proprietary components vertical integration) but commoditization risk from SpaceX pricing. 2.5% annual dilution consistent with current ~$250-350M/yr equity raises.
risks: Neutron delayed to 2027-2028, limiting TAM capture during critical SpaceX dominance window
Space systems margins compress as government contract mix shifts to fixed-price awards

bull.rationale: Bull catalyst: Neutron successfully reaches orbit by late 2026 / early 2027 and wins 3+ major constellation contracts (e.g. SDA, Kuiper, OneWeb successor), rapidly expanding TAM from $500M to $5B+ addressable market. Combined with Photon spacecraft platform scaling and Space Systems doubling revenues, total revenues reach $3B. Net margin of 14% achievable via Neutron's superior launch economics (partially reusable, ~$50-80M per flight vs Falcon 9 at $70M) driving 50%+ gross margins. Exit P/E of 75x — premium to aerospace peer average (18x) justified by execution of Neutron; analogous to SpaceX comps at ~100x EV/EBITDA. Quality multiplier 1.1: two moat sources emerge (proprietary vertical-integration of components + Neutron reusability moat if achieved). 2.0% annual dilution assumes company approaches FCF breakeven by 2028, reducing equity raise dependency.
risks: Valuation re-rates downward sharply if Neutron faces delays even in bull scenario
SpaceX enters small-sat launch market more aggressively, compressing Electron pricing

aiThesis.rationale: RKLB is a high-conviction SELL from a fundamental DCF perspective. At $143.48/share, the market is pricing in a best-case Neutron execution scenario — the stock is already 38% above the analyst mean target of $103.91. Our probability-weighted fair value of $10.46 implies -92.7% downside when applying standard DCF methodology (10% discount rate, 5-year horizon). Even in the pure bull scenario (38% CAGR, 14% net margin, 75x exit P/E, Neutron success), fair value is only $33.80 — still -76% below current price. This is a momentum/narrative stock trading on the optionality of Neutron success and space infrastructure themes, not on current or near-term fundamentals. The company will not achieve GAAP profitability before 2027 at best. For the Space & Defense sub-strategy, RKLB is a WATCHLIST-only name — do not initiate at current levels. Re-evaluate if price pulls back below $25-30 (approaching bull-case fundamental value) or if Neutron successfully reaches orbit and wins commercial contracts (thesis confirmation event).

analyticsLog.marginAnchor: TTM used as anchor for gross margin trend (trending: 9%→21%→26.6%→34.4% — consistent 4-year expansion). Net margin still deeply negative so projecting path to profitability from operating leverage thesis.
analyticsLog.growthDerivation: Hypergrowth exception applied (Y1 consensus +51.4% > 40% threshold). Y1=$910.8M (+51.4%), Y2=$1,282M (+40.8%), Y3~+28% (natural deceleration halving), Y4~+20%, Y5~+15% → 5-yr CAGR = (Y5rev/TTMrev)^(1/5)-1. Base: ~28% CAGR. Bear: 18% (execution delays, Electron-only growth). Bull: 38% (Neutron successful, catalytic constellation wins).
analyticsLog.sectorBenchmarkRow: Industrials row — Conservative P/E: 14, Median P/E: 18, Growth P/E: 24. RKLB exits above Growth P/E due to space-tech premium; explicitly justified in scenario rationale (Neutron catalyst, vertical integration moat).
dataQualityFlags: Deeply unprofitable company — EPS-based DCF has limited reliability at current stage; P/S ratio (138x) is the primary market-observed metric but not used to anchor fair value
